Rashi on Temurah 5a:10:1.hebrew: ולאביי - דאמר דכל מילתא דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד, מהני. הכא, בתורם מן הרעה על היפה, למאי הלכתא איצטריך למכתב "ולא תשאו עליו חטא", דמשמע דמהני:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:10:1.english: And according to Abaye - Who said that any matter about which the Merciful One said "do not do it," [the act] is effective. Here, in the case of one who separates teruma from the inferior produce for the superior, for what halakha was it necessary to write "And you shall bear no sin by reason of it," which implies that [the separation] is effective?

Rashi on Temurah 5a:10:2.english: The optimal [manner] - One separates teruma from the best [produce].

Rashi on Temurah 5a:10:3.english: He is not called a sinner - For there is nothing but a mere prohibition.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:10:4.hebrew: קמ"ל - הכתוב "ולא תשאו עליו חטא", דאפי' חוטא מיקרי:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:10:4.english: It teaches us - the verse "And you shall bear no sin by reason of it" — that he is even called a sinner.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:11:1.hebrew: ליתן חלב לזה וחלב לזה - דלהכי כתיב "חלב" "חלב" תרי זימני, חד בתירוש וחד ביצהר, לאשמועינן דיתן חלב לזה, שיפריש בפני עצמו מן המובחר של זה, כגון ממין על מינו, דהיינו יצהר על יצהר:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:11:1.english: To give the best of this one and the best of that one - For this is why "best" is written twice, once by the wine and once by the oil: to teach us that one must give the best for this one, meaning that he separates, on its own, from the choicest of this [type], for example from a type for its own type, that is, oil for oil:

Rashi on Temurah 5a:11:2.hebrew: וחלב לזה - מתירוש על תירוש, ולא ממין על שאינו מינו, כגון מיצהר על תירוש, ומתירוש על יצהר:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:11:2.english: And the best of the other - [One separates] from wine for wine, but not from one type for a different type, for example, from oil for wine, or from wine for oil.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:11:3.hebrew: אין תרומתו תרומה, אלמא לא מהני, וקשיא לאביי - שהוא דאמר מהני:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:11:3.english: His teruma is not teruma. Apparently it is not effective, and this is difficult for Abaye - who said that it is effective.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:12:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאמר קרא ראשיתם - כלומר, דשנה עליו הכתוב לעכב, דלא יתרום ממין על שאינו מינו. ואהכי, אם תרם — לא מהני:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:12:1.english: It is different there, as the verse says "the first part of them" - That is to say, the verse repeated it in this case in order to make it indispensable, so that one may not separate [teruma] from one type of produce for a different type. And therefore, if he did separate [it], it is not effective:

Rashi on Temurah 5a:12:2.hebrew: וכן אמר רבי אילעא - דלהכי לא מהני הפרשת תרומה ממין אחד על מין אחר, משום דראשיתם כתיב, דשנה עליו הכתוב לעכב:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:12:2.english: And so said Rabbi Ile'a - That for this reason [separating teruma from one kind for another kind] is not effective: because "their first part" is written, for the verse repeated it [the law] in order to make it indispensable.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:13:1.hebrew:
ולרבא - דאמר לא מהני לדידיה, אמאי איצטריך למכתב "ראשיתם"? משום דלא מהני?
ומשיב: אמר לך רבא: איצטריך למכתב "ראשיתם", דאי לא, הוה אמינא "חלב חלב" — אין תורמין מזה על זה:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:13:1.english:
And according to Rava - who said that it is not effective for him, why was it necessary to write "the first part of them"? Is it because it is not effective?
The Gemara answers: Rava could say to you: It was necessary to write "the first part of them," for if not, I would have said that "best…best" teaches that one may not separate teruma from this type for that type.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:15:1.hebrew: ה"ג אבל תירוש ודגן דחד חלב כתיב בהו - כלומר, דבין תירוש ודגן לא כתיב אלא חד חלב, דכתיב "וכל חלב תירוש ודגן". אימא דמצי תרם מהאי אהאי — מדגן על תירוש, ומתירוש על דגן, ודגן על דגן, דכולהו מיני דגנים, מזה על זה, כגון חטה על שעורה. להכי הדר כתב רחמנא "ראשיתם" כו':
Rashi on Temurah 5a:15:1.english: This is the correct reading: "But as for wine and grain, with regard to which 'best' is written once" - That is, between wine and grain, only one "best" is written, as it is written: "And all the best of the wine and the grain." One might say that one can separate teruma from this for that — from grain for wine, from wine for grain, and from grain for grain, since all the types of grain [count as one], from this one for that one, for example from wheat for barley. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote again: "The first part of them," etc.:

Rashi on Temurah 5a:16:1.english: Dedications of the priests - Dedications of an Israelite that are given to the priests:

Rashi on Temurah 5a:16:2.hebrew: אלמא לא מהניא - דאם פדאן, לא עשה ולא כלום, כדקתני: אין להם פדיון:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:16:2.english: Apparently, it is not effective - For if one redeemed them, he did nothing at all, as it teaches: They have no redemption.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:17:1.hebrew: בהווייתו - שאינו יוצא לחולין על ידי פדיון:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:17:1.english: As it is - For it does not go out to non-sacred status by means of redemption.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:1:1.hebrew: הא נמי לילקי - כלומר, תינח לאביי, דאמר דהיכא דמהני לילקי — להכי קתני הכא דאינו לוקה, דהא לא מהני מאי דעבד, שיכול להחזירה. אלא לרבא, דאמר דלא מהני, והאי דלקי משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא — הכא, אע"ג דלא מהני, לילקי נמי משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:1:1.english: This one too should be flogged - That is, this works out well according to Abaye, who says that [one is flogged] only where [the divorce] is effective; therefore it teaches here that he is not flogged, since what he did is not effective, as he can remarry her. But according to Rava, who says that [the divorce] is not effective, and that [the offender] is flogged because he violated the statement of the Merciful One — here too, even though [the divorce] is not effective, he should be flogged, because he violated the statement of the Merciful One.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:2:1.hebrew: לא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו - דמשמע דכל ימיו לא יוכל לשלחה, דאם גירש — יחזיר, דכל ימיו בעמוד והחזיר קאי. והילכך לא עבר אמימרא דרחמנא. אבל בעלמא, אע"ג דלא מהני, ודאי לוקה, משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:2:1.english: He may not send her away all his days - For it implies that all his days he may not send her away, [in the sense that] if he divorced her, he must take her back, since for all his days he stands under the obligation to arise and remarry her. And therefore he did not transgress the word of the Merciful One. But in other cases, even though [the divorce] is not effective, he certainly is flogged, because he transgressed the word of the Merciful One:

Rashi on Temurah 5a:3:1.hebrew: ולאביי - דאמר דהיכא דמהני לקי, אבל אי לא מהני לא לקי, לדידיה למאי איצטריך למיכתב "כל ימיו"? לאשמועינן דקאי בעמוד והחזיר? ואהכי לא לקי משום דהוי קום עשה? אפי' לא כתיב "כל ימיו" שמעינן לדידיה דלא לקי, כיון דלא מהני, דיכול להחזירה:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:3:1.english: And according to Abaye - who says that where [the act] is effective, he is flogged, but where it is not effective, he is not flogged: according to him, why is it necessary to write "all his days"? Is it to teach us that he stands in the position of "arise and return her"? And is this why he is not flogged, because it is an act of "arise and do"? Even if "all his days" were not written, we would learn, according to him, that he is not flogged, since [the divorce] is not effective, as he can [still] remarry her:

Rashi on Temurah 5a:3:2.hebrew: איסורא עבד לה - שגירשה, אבל מילקא לא לקי, והרשות בידו: ואי בעי ליהדר, ואי לא בעי לא ליהדר:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:3:2.english: He committed a prohibition against her - by divorcing her. But he would not be flogged, and the choice is in his hands: if he wants, he may remarry her, and if he does not want, he need not remarry her.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:3:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - "כל ימיו", ולימד לך הכתוב דחובה בידו להחזירה. והשתא, "כל ימיו" בעמוד והחזר קאי, והלכך לא לקי, ולאו משום דהוי קום עשה:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:3:3.english: It teaches us - "All his days," and the verse taught you that it is an obligation upon him to remarry her. And now, "all his days" stands in the category of "stand up and return" [i.e., a positive command to act], and therefore he does not receive lashes, and this is not because it is a "rise and do" [positive act] case.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:6:1.hebrew: ורבא אמר לך - כלומר, לרבא דאמר דכל לא תעשה שבתורה לא מהני לדידיה, למאי הלכתא איצטריך למיכתב "כל ימיו"? לאשמועינן דקאי בעמוד והחזר? פשיטא, דבכל דוכתא נמי שהוא לא תעשה לא מהני! ומשני רבא: אי לא כתיב "כל ימיו", הוה אמינא לילקי משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא, והדר ניהדר לה, כלומר שיהא מחזירה לאחר שילקה:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:6:1.english: And Rava could say to you - That is, according to Rava, who says that any prohibition in the Torah does not accomplish [anything] for him, for what halakhic purpose was it necessary to write "all his days"? To teach us that he stands [in the obligation] "stand and take her back"? It is obvious, since in every place where it is a prohibition it does not accomplish [anything] either! And Rava answers: If "all his days" had not been written, I would have said that he should be flogged because he transgressed the word of the Merciful One, and then he should take her back — that is, that he would take her back after he has been flogged.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:6:2.hebrew: והוה ליה אונס - כלומר, להכי תיסק אדעתין דלילקי, דהוי אונס דעובר אלאו דלא יוכל לשלחה, וליכא אלא לאו גרידתא. להכי כתיב "כל ימיו", דכל ימיו בעמוד והחזר קאי, דלא הוי לאו גרידתא, דהא אית ביה קום עשה, ולא לקי. ולהך לישנא הויא הכי כולה מסקנא דשמעתא:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:6:2.english: And it would be [a case of] a rapist - That is to say: Therefore it would have entered our mind that he should be flogged, since [the case of] a rapist is one who transgresses the prohibition of “he may not send her away,” and there is nothing here but a mere prohibition. Therefore it is written “all his days,” for “all his days” refers to [the requirement to] stand and take her back, so that it is not a mere prohibition, since it contains a positive commandment [to be fulfilled], and he is not flogged. And according to this version, the entire conclusion of the passage is as follows.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:8:1.hebrew: חלבו אין - מלמד שיהא תורם מן היפה על היפה:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:8:1.english: “Its choicest, yes” - This teaches that one must separate teruma from the best produce for the best produce.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:8:2.hebrew: גרוע לא - מן הגרוע, כגון מן הרע על היפה, הוא דאינו תורם, והיינו מילתא דקאמר רחמנא לא ליעביד. ולאו משום דהוי לאו ממש, אלא לאו הבא מכלל עשה הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:8:2.english: “Poor-quality, no” - It is from poor-quality produce, such as from the inferior for the superior, that one may not separate teruma; and this is the matter that the Merciful One said not to do. And this is not because it is an actual negative commandment, but rather it is a negative commandment derived from a positive commandment.

Rashi on Temurah 5a:8:3.hebrew: תרומתו תרומה - אלמא דמהני, וקשיא לרבא דאמר לא מהני:
Rashi on Temurah 5a:8:3.english: His teruma is teruma - Apparently, [his action] is effective, and this is difficult for Rava, who said that it is not effective.

Tosafot on Temurah 5a:12:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאמר קרא ראשיתם ראשית לזה וראשית לזה - וא"ת, והרי בריש פ' בתרא דבכורות (דף נד:) דריש אביי האי קרא למעוטי דגן ודגן? וי"ל, דהך דרשא דהתם מ"ראשית" אתיא, והך דהכא מ"ראשיתם":
Tosafot on Temurah 5a:12:1.english: It is different there, as the verse states: "The first part of them [reishitam] — a first part for this and a first part for that" - If you ask: But at the beginning of the last chapter of Bekhorot (54b), Abaye derives from this verse [a teaching] to exclude [the case of] grain and grain [of the same type]? And one can answer: That derivation there comes from the word "reishit" ["first part"], whereas this one here comes from the word "reishitam" ["the first part of them"]:

Tosafot on Temurah 5a:13:1.hebrew: ולרבא אי לאו דאמר רחמנא ראשיתם כו' - וא"ת, והא בפרק בתרא דבכורות (שם) אמר: בלא ראשיתם נמי כל משמע, ודגן אחד לא מצית אמרת? וצ"ל דהך סוגיא דהכא אתיא כמאן דאמר דראשית איצטריך שפיר לדגן ודגן:
Tosafot on Temurah 5a:13:1.english: "And according to Rava, had the Merciful One not said 'the first part of them' etc." - And if you ask: But in the last chapter of Bekhorot (there) it says: Even without [the word] "the first part of them," the word "all" implies [inclusion], and you cannot say that [it refers to] one type of grain! And one must answer that this passage here follows the one who says that "first part" is indeed needed for [the case of] one grain and another grain:

Tosafot on Temurah 5a:1:1.hebrew: מיתיבי אונס שגירש אם ישראל הוא מחזיר ואינו לוקה - וס"ד דהשתא הא דאינו לוקה לאו מטעם ניתוק הוא, אלא משום דלא מהניא גירושין, דהא צריך להחזירה. ואי אמרת כיון דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא לקי, הא נמי לילקי, ותיובתא דרבא. בשלמא לאביי ניחא, דמשום הכי לא לקי, דלא מהני מעשיו. וא"ת כיון דלא מהני גירושין, ליחייב הבא עליה משום אשת איש אפי' קודם חזרה, וכהן נמי, אמאי לוקה ואינו מחזיר? הוה לן למימר דלא חל הגט כלל. וי"ל דאיתקש גירושין למיתה, כדאמר פרק קמא דקידושין: איתקש מיתה לגירושין, ה"נ איתקש גירושין למיתה: מה מיתה מוציאה מרשות הבעל, אף גירושין כו'. ומיהו להכי לא מהני, שאין שילוח זה לכל ימיו, שהרי הוא צריך להחזירה. ולא אסיק אדעתיה עתה דכל ימיו הוי ניתוק, משום דהוי לאו שקדמו עשה, ומש"ה פריך לרבא: כיון דלא מהני, לילקי:
Tosafot on Temurah 5a:1:1.english: The Gemara objects: "A rapist who divorced [his victim] — if he is an Israelite, he remarries her and is not flogged" - And [the Gemara] initially thought that the fact that he is not flogged is not because of [the principle of] severance, but because the divorce is ineffective, since he must take her back. "And if you say that since he transgressed the statement of the Merciful One he is flogged, this one too should be flogged" — this is a refutation of Rava. It works well according to Abaye, [who holds] that he is not flogged for this reason: because his action is not effective. And if you ask: Since the divorce is not effective, then one who has relations with her should be liable for [relations with] a married woman, even before he takes her back; and also in the case of a priest, why is he flogged and does not take her back? We should have said that the bill of divorce does not take effect at all. And one can answer that divorce was compared to death, as stated in the first chapter of Kiddushin: Death was compared to divorce, [and] so too divorce was compared to death — just as death removes [a woman] from the husband's domain, so too divorce, etc. But nevertheless, it is not effective here, because this sending away is not for all his days, since he must take her back. And [the Gemara] did not, at this point, consider that [the prohibition lasts] all his days [if he does not remarry her], which would constitute severance, since it is a negative commandment that is preceded by a positive commandment; and therefore it raises the objection against Rava: Since it is not effective, he should be flogged.

Tosafot on Temurah 5a:2:1.hebrew: אמר לך רבא שאני התם דאמר קרא כל ימיו כל ימיו בעמוד והחזיר קאי - והוי ניתוק גמור, ואין זה "לאו שקדמו עשה". דלהכי איצטריך "כל ימיו", שאין שילוח זה "כל ימיו". וה"ק קרא: לא יוכל לשלחה, ואם שלחה — לא יהא שילוח זה "כל ימיו", שהרי הוא צריך להחזירה. ואע"ג דאפשר להעמיד "כל ימיו" בלא שילוח, מ"מ כיון דלא כתיב "לו תהיה לאשה כל ימיו", וכתיב "כל ימיו" לאחר "לא יוכל לשלחה", שמע מינה דלניתוק ללאו כתביה. דזה הכלל: דכל היכא דיש הוכחה בקרא דעשה קאי אחר הלאו, אין זה "לאו שקדמו עשה". אבל מ"לו תהיה לאשה" בלא "כל ימיו" לא הוה דייק ליה בניתוק, שהרי "לו תהיה לאשה" מיירי בלא שילוח:
Tosafot on Temurah 5a:2:1.english: Rava could say to you: It is different there, as the verse states "all his days" — "all his days" — he stands [under the obligation to] arise and remarry her - And this is a complete severing [of the prohibition], and this is not a "prohibition that was preceded by a positive commandment." For this is why "all his days" was needed: that this sending away should not be "all his days." And this is what the verse is saying: He may not send her away, but if he did send her away, this sending away is not to be "all his days," since he must take her back. And although it is possible to explain "all his days" as applying without any sending away, nevertheless, since it is not written "she shall be a wife to him all his days," and "all his days" is written after "he may not send her away," we conclude that it was written to sever [the prohibition from its] negative commandment. For this is the rule: wherever there is proof in the verse that the positive commandment is connected to the prohibition, this is not a "prohibition that was preceded by a positive commandment." But from "she shall be a wife to him" without "all his days," we would not have inferred that it severs [the prohibition], since "she shall be a wife to him" speaks of a case without sending away:

Tosafot on Temurah 5a:9:1.hebrew: אם אינו קדוש נשיאות חטא למה - וא"ת נימא דנשיאות חטא הוי משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא? ואומר רבינו שמשון משנ"ץ: דה"פ אם אינו קדוש נשיאות חטא למה כתיב — בלאו הכי נמי ידעינן דיש בו נשיאות חטא, מדכתיב "מכל חלבו", דמשמע חלבו — אין, גירועין — לא:
Tosafot on Temurah 5a:9:1.english: "If it is not consecrated, why [would there be] bearing of sin?" - And if you say: Let us say that the bearing of sin is because he transgressed the word of the Merciful One? And Rabbeinu Shimshon of Sens says: This is its meaning: "If it is not consecrated, why [would there be] bearing of sin?" — why is [this verse] written? Even without it we would know that there is bearing of sin in it, since it is written "of all its best part," which implies [that taking from] its best part — yes [is required]; [taking from] inferior produce — no.
